output.diagnosis: Payment is blocked by an internal restructuring at the payer, not by ordinary lateness. The AP lead states payables for all group companies were moved to a single desk, that she has no visibility once the file leaves her system, and she cannot say who is holding it; payer notes add that approval limits were rewritten this month and queued items went back for fresh review. She offered to share a head-office address instead. Payment history shows four prior invoices settled in full, though consistently well past terms, including one settled the day before this snapshot, so the relationship appears to be paying rather than disputing. No dispute description, no promise-to-pay, and no contacts have been made on this invoice yet.
output.reasoning: The named contact has explicitly told us she is not the decision point and cannot report status, and the approval route has been redirected to an unnamed head office. Another automated chase to the same mailbox would land with someone who has already said she cannot act, so it is unlikely to move the file. What is needed is a human to obtain the head-office contact she offered, confirm the new approval path, and re-present the invoice into the reworked queue. The receivable is large and the payer is a group entity, which strengthens the case for human handling rather than an automated nudge. Uncertainty: the payer's own words are the only evidence for the restructuring, there is no stated timeline for the fresh review, and the consistent history of eventual full payment means this could simply resolve on its own; I am not treating the redirection as a commercial objection to the invoice itself.
